cases.question: Decode the final routing record for relay RL-27: which port, custodian, launch time, registry desk, clearance phrase, and final verifier does it specify?
cases.answer: RL-27 specifies Port Meridian, custodian Talia Nox, a 05:35 launch, registry Desk Cobalt, clearance phrase silver dawn, and final verifier Edda Marr.

truth_claims.claim: FINAL ROUTING ROW FOR RL-27 | Q4 | N7 | H3
the registry desk is Desk Cobalt
the clearance phrase is silver dawn
the final verifier is Edda Marr

turns.content: A superseded routing sheet wrote RL-27 in plain text as Port Auburn, custodian Jaro Wen, launch 04:10. It is retained only for audit comparison.
Relay RL-72 uses Port Meridian for a 04:10 launch, but its custodian is Jaro Wen. RL-72 is unrelated to the requested row.
A rehearsal card mentions RL-27 and asks trainees to compare Q2, N4, and H8. The card contains no authorized routing row.

Signed relay ledger, revision seven. This ledger is encoded to keep repeated routing rows compact. The preliminary notes below document checksum handling and do not assign a relay. Checksum groups are copied twice, separator bars have no semantic value, and rehearsal annotations are non-authoritative. Archive staff must use only the notation key and the row marked FINAL. The ledger remains controlling until a later signed revision is issued.
Notation key for this signed ledger: Q4 means Port Meridian. N7 means Talia Nox. H3 means 05:35. Other code families belong to unrelated ledgers and must not be imported.

Interleaf preservation record. Conservators inspected the cover cloth, endpaper fibers, binding cord, watermark position, page-edge wear, folio sequence, ink oxidation, staple holes, scanner focus, envelope wax, storage temperature, humidity tape, courier receipts, witness initials, duplication count, optical density, paper thickness, barcode alignment, cabinet shelf marks, and checksum typography. A second conservator repeated the inspection against the sealed archive copy and found every physical characteristic unchanged. This interleaf describes document condition only and contains no routing identifier, encoded assignment, field role, or operational value.

RL-27 audit marker alpha confirms that the relay identifier survived the checksum copy. It does not restate or decode the route fields. Archive verification records separator counts, envelope seals, witness initials, folio edges, scanner calibration, paper stock, duplicate signatures, ink density, receipt numbers, parity groups, and checksum rotation. Every listed item is administrative evidence only; none names a port, a custodian, or a launch time. This marker exists solely to make later corruption detectable for RL-27.

RL-27 audit marker beta confirms that three encoded fields follow the identifier. The verification worksheet inventories binding stitches, transfer receipts, page impressions, barcode parity, seal colors, cabinet temperatures, witness initials, duplicate folios, optical alignment, archive humidity, checksum columns, and paper grain. Those observations neither decode nor replace any field in the routing row. They certify only that the signed revision remained physically intact while RL-27 moved through the archive.

RL-27 audit marker gamma says that the controlling final routing row follows after this audit section. Its validation trail records courier receipts, signature counts, seal impressions, folio sequence, archive shelf moves, scanner density, binding tension, checksum witnesses, duplicate-page comparison, and envelope numbering. Training cards and the superseded plain-text sheet are excluded. None of these audit facts identifies the requested port, custodian, or launch time for RL-27.
FINAL ROUTING ROW FOR RL-27 | Q4 | N7 | H3 | port, custodian, and launch-time fields use the earlier notation key
RL-27 supplemental current field: the registry desk is Desk Cobalt.

cases.question: Interpret the accepted matrix record for chamber CX-8: what coolant, duty cycle, reviewer, sensor band, restart key, and records custodian are assigned?
cases.answer: CX-8 uses coolant Selene, a 36-minute duty cycle, reviewer Omar Vey, sensor band Pine-4, restart key ember lattice, and records custodian Nira Sol.

truth_claims.claim: ACCEPTED MATRIX ROW FOR CX-8 :: S2 :: D6 :: R9
the restart key is ember lattice
the records custodian is Nira Sol

A simulator worksheet for CX-8 combines S5, D2, and R1. It is not an accepted chamber matrix.
Reviewer Omar Vey observes CX-3 during a 36-minute stress test with coolant Orin; the test is not an assignment.

Accepted thermal matrix, calibration cycle eleven. Introductory calibration notes describe checksum columns, redundant delimiters, sensor tolerances, and audit signatures. None of those notes assign a chamber. Only the codebook in this source and the row marked ACCEPTED jointly determine the live assignment.
Codebook: S2 decodes to coolant Selene. D6 decodes to a 36-minute duty cycle. R9 decodes to reviewer Omar Vey. Codes from draft or simulator matrices are not compatible.
